haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, with an outbox row in the same transaction. Then the instance copies to Postgres inline with a 250 ms timeout. A Postgres failure only logs; the request still succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: Only if the incoming row's version is higher than the stored row's version, and no tombstone exists for that id.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must report dual_mysql_primary, with series count equal to instance count, on the new code, and the outbox draining, for 2 minutes. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s.
haiku-low.q4: It pauses 10 s and rechecks whenever replica lag is above 5 s or unavailable, reads 2000-row batches, and sleeps a throttle interval. That interval is not yet set.
haiku-low.q5: Reads move after the step 8 comparison is clean. The source of truth moves only after a 72-hour soak at 100% reads with clean nightly runs, a nearly empty outbox, and a rehearsed runbook.
haiku-low.q6: The outbox row, committed with the change in the source-of-truth store's outbox table. The sync worker copies it to the other store, retrying forever with backoff capped at 60 s.
haiku-low.q7: Every copy checks for a tombstone before writing, and erasure writes the tombstone in the same transaction as the delete. Tombstones are kept until the MySQL table is dropped.
haiku-low.q8: In the backfill row of migration_progress, with last_id updated in the same transaction as each batch. It stops when the cursor passes max(id) and the outbox is empty, then a final pass runs and status becomes done.
haiku-low.q9: The comparison job, over 100,000-id ranges. It rechecks mismatches against the MySQL primary after about 10 s, and confirmed mismatches are inserted into the outbox for automatic repair.
haiku-low.q10: Closing the MySQL fence makes stale-flag instances get retryable 503s, so no split brain. If the switch runs past T0+40 s, reopen the MySQL fence and leave the flag unchanged.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns ids from a sequence set to MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT value, not max+1, so freed ids are never reused. Before rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT must exceed the maximum Postgres id, raised if not.
haiku-low.q12: Dual writes copy every Postgres change back to MySQL through the Postgres outbox. Rollback closes the Postgres fence, drains its outbox, checks AUTO_INCREMENT, sets dual_mysql_primary, and reopens the MySQL fence. It ends at step 13, switching to pg_only.

sonnet.q1: MySQL (SoT) commits first, in a transaction that also inserts an outbox row. After commit the instance tries the Postgres copy inline (250 ms timeout, try/except). If Postgres fails, it only logs; the request still succeeds, the caller sees success.
sonnet.q2: Only if the incoming version is higher than the stored row's version (version rule: insert if missing, or replace if stored version < incoming), and no tombstone exists for the id. Same for inline, backfill, repair copies.
sonnet.q3: Step 5 gate, held at least 2 minutes: app_flag_value for users_write_mode reads dual_mysql_primary on every instance, with reporting series count equal to instance count; no instance runs old code; the outbox is draining. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change (cache refresh every 30 s).
sonnet.q4: Backfill reads from the MySQL replica in batches of 2000 and sleeps a throttle interval between batches (interval not yet set; pick in staging). Before each batch it checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds; if above 5 or unavailable it sleeps 10 s and rechecks.
sonnet.q5: Reads to Postgres: backfill finished (step 7) and the full comparison passed clean (step 8: complete run after step 7 with confirmed_mismatches = 0); then ramp 1, 10, 50, 100% with at least 30 min per stage. SoT switch: soak passed (72 h continuous at 100% reads with every nightly comparison clean), outbox nearly empty, and a named operator ready with the runbook scripted and rehearsed in staging.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (users_sync_outbox), inserted in the same transaction as the change on the SoT (MySQL), records it durably. The sync worker polls the outbox every second, reads the current user from the SoT primary, applies it to Postgres, retries forever with backoff capped at 60 s, and deletes the claimed outbox rows. Alert if oldest row is over 5 minutes.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: the erasure job deletes the user and inserts a users_tombstone row in one transaction on the SoT. Every copy statement (inline, backfill, repair) applies only if no tombstone exists for the id, so a stale copy cannot resurrect the user. Tombstones are kept until the MySQL table is dropped.
sonnet.q8: In the migration_progress table (the backfill row, last_id cursor) in Postgres. The cursor is updated in the same Postgres transaction as the batch apply, so a crash continues exactly after the last completed batch; a lease keeps one runner active. It stops when the cursor passes the MySQL max(id) and outbox backlog is empty, then one more pass up to the current max id catches new rows, and status is set to done.
sonnet.q9: The comparison job (users-compare): walks id ranges of 100,000 comparing (id, version, hash of email, name, plan, updated_at) between the MySQL replica and Postgres primary; finds missing, extra, differing ids and ids both user and tombstone. After about 10 s it re-checks each mismatch against the MySQL primary, skipping ids with a pending outbox row. Still-mismatched ids are confirmed and each inserted into the outbox so repair is automatic. It also reruns nightly.
sonnet.q10: The write fence: a write_fence table on each store, locked FOR SHARE by every write transaction. Closing the MySQL fence waits for in-flight writes and blocks later ones; a stale-flag instance hits the closed fence and gets a retryable 503 (WritesPaused), so it can never write to the old SoT. Flag change and opening the Postgres fence happen together. If it runs long, abort deadline T0+40 s: reopen the MySQL fence and leave the flag alone; nothing has changed. Worst case pause about 70 s, under the 90 s limit.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids from a sequence set (setval) to MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT value (read from information_schema.tables with information_schema_stats_expiry=0), not max(id)+1, so a freed top id is never reused (protects tombstones). On rollback, step 3 checks that MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is above the maximum Postgres id and raises it if not (InnoDB also raises its counter when a larger explicit id is inserted).
sonnet.q12: After the switch (dual_pg_primary), writes commit in Postgres with a Postgres outbox row and are copied to MySQL under the same version/tombstone rules; the worker and nightly comparison keep running; alert if Postgres outbox older than 30 s. Rollback (any time before step 13): close Postgres fence, drain Postgres outbox to zero, check/raise MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT above max Postgres id, set users_write_mode=dual_mysql_primary and open the MySQL fence, abort at T0+40 s. Postgres keeps receiving copies. Limit: cannot finish while Postgres is down. The option ends at step 13 (pg_only), after at least 14 days, 3 clean comparison runs and empty outbox; after that rollback needs a new backfill from Postgres.
